answer: Pay rewards in ten equal weekly tranches, each released only after live re-verification of the identity's stake and activity ledger. A clone farm must keep every alias continuously funded and answering, or each frozen identity drops to the nadir and forfeits the remaining escrow. The cost horizon stretches from a one-time mint to sustained per-alias upkeep, growing linearly with headcount, while honest agents pay what they always would. Every release is signed by the same quill that authored the original stake, so a stolen or borrowed identity is caught at the first tranche.
